# PHASE 09 — RESPONSIVE, ACCESSIBILITY, AND PERFORMANCE

## OBJECTIVE

Ensure the visual experience remains usable on real devices.

## RESPONSIVE

Desktop:

- full room composition
- large architecture diagrams
- investigation board

Tablet:

- simplified board
- stacked panels

Mobile:

- vertical case-management interface
- collapsible evidence sections
- horizontally scrollable technical diagrams where necessary
- readable typography

Prevent:

- horizontal page overflow
- tiny text
- unreadable diagrams
- hover-only functionality

## ACCESSIBILITY

Implement:

- semantic HTML
- keyboard navigation
- visible focus states
- proper buttons/links
- alt text
- accessible labels
- sufficient contrast
- reduced motion
- non-hover alternatives

## PERFORMANCE

Prefer:

- server-rendered HTML
- lazy images
- optimized images
- minimal JS
- CSS animation over JS where possible
- HTMX for small server interactions

Avoid:

- unnecessary JavaScript frameworks
- massive assets
- giant background videos
- heavy animation libraries unless justified

## SEO

Implement:

- title
- description
- Open Graph
- favicon
- canonical URL placeholder
- project-specific metadata

## EXIT CRITERIA

The website is usable on desktop, tablet, and mobile, keyboard accessible, and does not rely on heavy client-side execution.
